# Espoo Kurttila mast — OCV-Paper, figures A–E

*Espoo · event-free control site · 150 acquisitions · 2024-09-05 … 2026-09-07 · generated by `code/espoo/fig_espoo_ocv_paper.py`*

## The question

This record has **no ground-truth state label** — no `damage_label`, no `structural_state`, no `condition_label` on any of its 150 rows — and the committed upstream verdict says so in its own words. There is therefore no severity axis to regress against. The only contrast the record supports is the one between its two **orbit geometries**:

* **ASCENDING — ascending orbit, afternoon pass** (n = 70)
* **DESCENDING — descending orbit, morning pass** (n = 80)

The observability core vector of the site is `OCV = [gamma2, A]` — interferometric coherence gamma^2 and `A` = `coherence_masked_pixels`, the size of the coherent echo mask. The question of this figure set is not *whether an event can be seen* (there is none declared and none in the window) but **how large the geometry effect is against the record's own no-event controls** — which is exactly the baseline any damage claim at another site has to beat.

## What each panel shows

### A — raw distributions

| channel | ASC (n=70) | DESC (n=80) |
|---|---|---|
| coherence  gamma^2 | 0.1746 | 0.02575 |
| mask area  A  [px] | 6 | 11 |

The two distributions barely overlap: gamma^2 sits at 0.1746 on ASC against 0.02575 on DESC, while the mask is *smaller* on ASC (6 px) than on DESC (11 px). A compact, highly coherent echo against a wide, incoherent one — a geometry signature, not a damage signature. Panel (c) adds the phase ladder, which exists for only 80 of 150 acquisitions (53.3 %) and for 0 of them carries an SNR at all.

### B — in-sample effect sizes

| channel | Cliff's delta (DESC − ASC) | bootstrap 95 % CI | SDS | n ASC |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `gamma2` | -0.7521 | [-0.8493, -0.6389] | 7.521 | 70 |
| `A` | 0.3055 | [0.1259, 0.4789] | 3.055 | 70 |
| `phase_coherence` | -0.02689 | [-0.2896, 0.2345] | 0.2689 | 39 |
| `phase_rms_rad` | 0.2058 | [-0.0469, 0.4434] | 2.058 | 39 |
| `wind_speed_ms` *(control)* | -0.06571 | [-0.1657, 0.03911] | 0.6571 | 70 |
| `temperature_c` *(control)* | -0.004643 | [-0.1075, 0.0986] | 0.04643 | 70 |

The orbit test on gamma^2: Welch t = 7.31, p = 2.71e-10, Mann-Whitney p = 2.16e-15. The geometry contrast is the largest effect in the record — larger than any season stratum (panel B b) and larger than either weather co-variate (panel E c).

### C — is the geometry learnable from the two measured channels?

| model | accuracy | balanced accuracy | p (accuracy) | p (balanced) | n |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `gamma2` — gamma2 | 0.7467 | 0.7321 | 0.000999 | 0.000999 | 150 |
| `A` — A | 0.6 | 0.6143 | 0.01499 | 0.001998 | 150 |
| `gamma2A` — gamma2+A | 0.74 | 0.7259 | 0.000999 | 0.000999 | 150 |
| `x_cov` — gamma2+A+wx | 0.7467 | 0.7339 | 0.000999 | 0.000999 | 150 |

Chance is **0.5** (two classes, balanced accuracy). Leave-one-out over the whole record — the labels are never shuffled, so the number is honest; the permutation null only quantifies how surprising it is.

### D — the headline pair across the four feature sets, and out of time

| model | delta (out-of-fold) | SDS | p (permutation of SDS) | paired CI of the SDS difference vs gamma^2 | SDS (out-of-time) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `gamma2` — gamma2 | 0.7307 | 7.307 | 0.07393 | -- | 7.332 |
| `A` — A | 0.2539 | 2.539 | 0.2398 | [-6.372, -3.211] | 2.964 |
| `gamma2A` — gamma2+A | 0.6757 | 6.757 | 0.02298 | [-1.075, -0.1071] | 6.754 |
| `x_cov` — gamma2+A+wx | 0.6857 | 6.857 | 0.00999 | [-1.021, 0.06429] | 6.871 |

The out-of-time split cuts the record in half by acquisition order (75 / 75, split at 2025-09-06) and scores each half with the model fitted on the other one. The second channel and the two weather co-variates add nothing that survives the split: the honest reading is that the *orbit* is separable and the *geometry* is all the vector measures.

### E — the four no-event controls

**E1 stationarity.** 13 of 14 committed phase-coherence series are stationary by the tests the site itself applies (Theil-Sen slope with a moving-block bootstrap CI, Mann-Kendall, first/second-half split, annual harmonic, lag-1 autocorrelation, runs test and Ljung-Box on the detrended series). The one series carrying a flag is `8-18 Hz · full_burst · ASCENDING` (trend, split_shift). A stationary series is the *precondition* for a persistence channel, not a persistence channel.

| series | n | median | trend /yr | MK p | split delta | flags |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `1-3 Hz · full_burst · ASCENDING` | 69 | 0.172 | -0.0007155 | 0.7837 | -0.1765 | — |
| `1-3 Hz · full_burst · DESCENDING` | 76 | 0.1718 | 0.001851 | 0.4017 | 0.1282 | — |
| `3-8 Hz · full_burst · ASCENDING` | 69 | 0.1082 | 0.001405 | 0.3593 | -0.003361 | — |
| `3-8 Hz · full_burst · DESCENDING` | 76 | 0.1075 | -0.002421 | 0.15 | -0.1753 | — |
| `3-8 Hz · strip400_annotation · ASCENDING` | 69 | 0.2403 | -0.0004825 | 0.9628 | 0.05882 | — |
| `3-8 Hz · strip400_annotation · DESCENDING` | 76 | 0.2078 | 0.001756 | 0.8261 | 0.0894 | — |
| `3-8 Hz · strip400_pipeline · ASCENDING` | 69 | 0.2474 | 0.004099 | 0.7442 | 0.08235 | — |
| `3-8 Hz · strip400_pipeline · DESCENDING` | 76 | 0.2165 | -0.004557 | 0.4593 | -0.1019 | — |

| `8-18 Hz · full_burst · DESCENDING` | 76 | 0.07291 | -0.0002269 | 0.8121 | -0.02564 | — |

| `8-18 Hz · strip400_pipeline · DESCENDING` | 76 | 0.1443 | -0.002574 | 0.5389 | -0.04089 | — |

Five of the committed fields of these blocks — `dwell_s`, `n_sub`, `nyquist_hz`, `n_observable` and `dwell_control` — are **not** re-derivable from the committed series (a series is a list of `[day, value]` pairs), so the pin block compares them for internal consistency and says so; every other field of every one of the 14 series is recomputed and pinned field by field.

**E2 month and season.** There is no event to cut on, so the record is split by season and by month instead. Every season reproduces the same sign and roughly the same size, which is what a geometry effect looks like.

| season | n | delta gamma^2 | delta A |
|---|---|---|---|
| `shoulder_Aug-Sep` | 30 | -0.6356 | 0.2889 |
| `summer_Mar-Jul` | 60 | -0.8653 | 0.3827 |
| `winter_Oct-Feb` | 60 | -0.6786 | 0.2444 |

**E3 wind and temperature.** The weather columns of this export are constant over long stretches, so the contrast is not *corrected* for them — it is recomputed **inside** each distinct value, which is the strongest form of the control available here.

| pair | n | Spearman rho | p |
|---|---|---|---|
| `gamma2` vs `wind_speed_ms` | 150 | 0.009973 | 0.9036 |
| `gamma2` vs `temperature_c` | 150 | 0.0419 | 0.6107 |
| `A` vs `wind_speed_ms` | 150 | 0.01199 | 0.8842 |
| `A` vs `temperature_c` | 150 | 0.03385 | 0.6809 |

| stratum | n | ASC / DESC | delta gamma^2 | bootstrap 95 % CI |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| wind = 5 | 132 | 62 / 70 | -0.7479 | [-0.8521, -0.6327] |
| temperature = 10 | 132 | 62 / 70 | -0.7479 | [-0.8521, -0.6327] |

Pooled delta gamma^2 = -0.7521. Every stratum with enough acquisitions on both sides keeps the same sign; none inverts it, so weather does not explain the geometry effect.

## What this control says

At a site with **no event at all**, the observability core vector still splits its record into two groups that are almost perfectly separable — and the split is the **orbit geometry**, not a state of the structure. That is the point of including Espoo in this repository:

1. an effect size of 7.31 (Welch t) and a leave-one-out balanced accuracy of 0.7259 look like *damage* under any classifier-first reading;
2. the record's own no-event controls (stationarity, season, weather, coverage) show every one of those numbers is geometry;
3. so at every other site of this repository the orbit-geometry contrast has to be reported **beside** the damage contrast before the latter can be read — which is exactly what the LUMO, Morandi, YWF and Carola packages do.

## Pins

Every committed number of this site is re-derived and compared: **all checks passed**.

| target | what is pinned |
|---|---|
| `espoo_ocv_channels.csv` | sha256 against the generator's own `output_sha256`, plus the source digest; `A` copied, not recomputed; 150 rows, 70 ASC / 80 DESC, 25 months, `2024-09-05` … `2026-09-07` |
| `espoo_mast_observability.json` | `per_pass`, `per_orbit`, `orbit_test`, `verdict.classes`, `constants`, `lumo_reference`, provenance and catalogue — field by field |
| `fig_espoo_channels.json` | the 15 pooled/per-orbit `{n, median}` blocks, the 25-month composition and the LUMO reference scale |
| `espoo_phase_stationarity.json` | all 14 series: median, IQR, Theil-Sen slope + bootstrap CI, Mann-Kendall, lag-1, runs test, Ljung-Box, half-split, annual harmonic, monthly means, flags and verdict — plus every number the file's own prose quotes |
| `espoo_ocv_findings.json` | this package's own derivation lock, re-derived and pinned field by field.

## Reproduce

```bash
python3 code/espoo/espoo_ocv_channels_csv.py       # rebuild + verify the table
python3 code/espoo/espoo_ocv_core.py               # read-only brief of the layer
python3 code/espoo/fig_espoo_ocv_paper.py          # figures A–E + this report
python3 code/espoo/fig_espoo_ocv_paper.py --quick  # without the permutation nulls
python3 code/espoo/fig_espoo_ocv_months.py         # the month companion
```

*environment: python 3.13.5, numpy 2.4.6, matplotlib 3.11.1*

*No wall-clock value appears in this file, so two runs of the same code produce identical bytes.*
